title: His mother's life, her flirting and death in 1961
summary: Gil says his mother had the real life. He describes her flirtatiousness, her last years with his brother and her love of travel.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: So actually she is the one you should be writing about. She had the life, I didn't have the life, she had the life.
Well I think that this an is/absolutely fascinating part of your background. And much about your mother is certainly legitimate. This is what..... or was it illegitimate uh? (LAUGHTER).

Because one of the aspects of being able to talk at least five hours here is that we do get a chance to bring out some things which one doesn't ordinarily get a chance to talk about. Some things that are inside that he really wants to explore. As I've said, these ridiculous tape shows that we look at so often on how did you get started and that sort of thing, is not what we are about. And they don't end up being very, very valuable at all.

But I think this kind of thing is because it gives us an insight into various kinds of social backgrounds. And here, we are particularly involved in what happened to a family that migrated from Australia.
I think your mother must have been a very beautiful woman or something to, you know, have acquired such an assortment of husbands including a doctor.
She was really a flirt you know. She flirted when she ninety. She was still flirting, right? And men were still proposing to her.
Oh dear. How old was she when she died?
Well over the period of years, were you in close touch with her?
Well the last few years she was living with my brother. He was in San Jose. He went and got her. She was living in (Balboa?) by herself. He felt like she shouldn't be living by herself.
But it didn't turn out to be such a good idea I don't really think. But I was attending ( ) so I couldn't do
anything about it. So my brother took her to San Jose and she lived there until she died.

She could only really, she could only go on doing what she wanted to do. Like the same thing, what she wanted to do, she didn't want to be cooped up like that in a house, you know. But she didn't have the where-withal that's all that mattered... that was the matter. If She had money she could have gone on and traveling. ?). She liked to do that.
In those days it took like six months to go from South Africa to India to Australia, I mean really those (British Isles?) people really got around ......
Oh yes, they'd lose a rudder and.....
Yes, they'd lose a rudder on the boat. She drifted once on an ocean liner. It might take a month or more between New Zealand and Durban at that time.
